reviews.feedback:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (5 objections, all sustained; 4 conceded in defense, 1 after rebuttal).

VERDICT ON THIS EVAL: keep, it is one of only four that discriminate. 0A1 and 0A3 are two of the
five sound with_skill flips, and both test script-interface quality (per-row interface column;
argv plus exit codes), not classification.

SKILL DEFECT, not an eval defect: 0A5 is the suite's other baseline-favouring flip. The with_skill
run classified step 7 ("verify entries clearly written") HYBRID and attached a script interface;
the baseline correctly kept it judgment. This compounds a defect iteration-1 verified and this
iteration reproduced: render_report.py:90-97 sums approx_tokens over SCRIPT *and* HYBRID and
prints it as "removes ~N tokens of per-run reasoning", while SKILL.md Step 8 explicitly RETAINS
HYBRID prose. This run printed "~181 tokens removed" with 2 of 7 steps HYBRID. Over-applying
HYBRID both misclassifies judgment work and inflates the advertised saving. Fix both together.

0A2 (no writes) passes in both arms; move it to the guardrail tier - collect_facts.py already
decides it from the tree diff.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: two of this eval's six assertions need replacing.

1A1 ">=3 Python scripts" FAILED BOTH ARMS (with_skill 2, baseline 1) -> zero information, and it
punishes the better engineering choice. The baseline's own report argued it: "Five scripts would
parse the folder five times and could disagree with each other." Replace with coverage, pinned to
the eval's pre-registered step set, NOT to what the arm classified (an arm-supplied denominator
rewards under-classification, the exact failure evals 0/4/8 exist to catch):
  "steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are each invoked by an exact command line in the rewritten SKILL.md, and
   every generated script exits 0 on --help."

1A3 "smoke-test PASS reported before the SKILL.md rewrite" is byte-identical to eval-6 A4, and the
two graders returned OPPOSITE verdicts on the same baseline evidence class. Ordering is
unobservable here: it can only be read from transcript-notes.md, authored by the agent under test,
which GRADER_INSTRUCTIONS.md elsewhere says to distrust; find over iteration-3 returns zero .jsonl,
so no independent tool-call record exists. Either persist per-run tool logs, or re-express as
end-state: "a manifest and fixtures exist for every generated script, and the smoke test exits 0
against the final on-disk state."

KEEP 1A4 - it is a genuine separator and a real defect in the baseline: with_skill exits 1 on
findings, the baseline reports the same finding and exits 0, reserving nonzero for a bad path. A
linter that exits 0 on findings cannot gate CI.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: 3/3 vs 3/3, all three assertions NON-DISCRIMINATING. Confirmed by diff -r
against the pristine fixture (exit 0 both arms) and check.py --help exit 0.

Costs 50,347 tokens with_skill and 37,443 baseline to tell you nothing about the skill. The
baseline independently reached the same 0-new-scripts verdict with the same classifications and
even found the same fixture gap.

DECISION: either retire it, or move all three assertions into the guardrail tier as a binary
regression gate against false-positive scripting - which is a real property worth protecting, just
not one that belongs in a pass-rate percentage. Do not leave it contributing to the headline,
where it inflates both arms toward 100% and hides where the signal is.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: this eval contains the suite's clearest inversion.

3A1 "exactly two generated scripts" is one of only TWO baseline-favouring flips in all 51
assertions, and it fires against the skill for making the better choice: with_skill merged steps 1
and 3 into one scan pass (correct - one parse, no chance of disagreement), the baseline wrote two
files. The suite is inconsistent about consolidation: eval 1 demands >=3, eval 3 exactly 2, eval 6
>=2, and it scores both directions depending on the eval.

Replace with: "the rewritten SKILL.md invokes a generated script at steps 1 and 3, and no other
step gained a script invocation." Invariant to consolidation, mechanically checkable, tests what
the eval actually cares about. Under that wording with_skill's FAIL likely becomes a PASS.

3A3 is a genuine separator worth keeping: with_skill's script exits 0 on --help and 2 on bad args
with 6/6 smoke checks green; BOTH baseline scripts exit 1 on --help with empty stdout, and a
no-arg run silently defaults to `changelogs` and exits 0.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: 4/4 vs 4/4, non-discriminating.

This eval guards a failure mode only scriptify can have - stalling at "0 steps extracted" on a
target with no numbered steps. The baseline has no step-extraction stage to fail at, so the eval
is a valid REGRESSION TEST for the skill but structurally incapable of producing a delta.

DECISION: keep it, but move it out of the pass-rate percentage and into the guardrail tier, where
a regression test belongs. Reporting it as 4/4 vs 4/4 inflates both arms and tells a reader
nothing.

Note 4A4 is DEFINITIONAL on vocabulary only: the baseline labels the step "Stays prose" rather
than "CLAUDE", with the same deadline reasoning. If any classification assertion is kept, grade
substance not the label token, as this grader did.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: 7/7 vs 6/7. The single separator is sound and worth keeping.

5A6 separated the arms on exit-code contracts: both arms classify steps 1/4/7 SCRIPT with concrete
argv, but the baseline states no exit-code contract anywhere (grep for exit/status: zero hits),
while with_skill gives 0/1/2 for every proposed script. That is a real interface guarantee - it is
what makes a generated script callable from another script without parsing stdout. This is a
better separator than iteration-1's, which merely rewarded scriptify's output schema.

The other six assertions are non-discriminating. The agent-tool trap - keeping WebFetch,
AskUserQuestion and the MCP call off pure SCRIPT - was handled correctly by BOTH arms, in this
iteration and in iteration-1. That trap is no longer earning its 3 assertions.

UNSCORED SIGNAL the suite misses: the with_skill run found two real defects in the fixture that no
assertion rewards - step 1's stated order (dedupe before lowercase) lets the case-variant duplicate
survive, and step 5 publishes to Notion before steps 6-7 produce the data.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: 5/6 vs 4/6, but the eval needs two repairs.

6A3 CONFLATES TWO PROPERTIES - ">=2 newly generated Python scripts AND each supports --help" - and
the count clause is HIDING A REAL SKILL WIN. Both arms wrote exactly 1 script, so both fail on
count. Underneath: with_skill's lint_docs.py --help exits 0 with argparse output; the baseline's
lint_docs_structure.py prints "not a directory: --help" and exits 2 from a hand-rolled parser.
Split the assertion and eval 6 goes from 5/6 vs 4/6 to 6/6 vs 4/6, measuring interface quality
instead of file count.

6A4 is byte-identical to eval-1 A3 and the two graders DISAGREED on the same evidence class - see
the eval-1 note. Ordering is unobservable in this harness; replace it.

6A1 (collision) passes in both arms - verified independently: check_headings.py is sha256
d60bc3d4... in both, byte-identical to baseline. The baseline unaided found that the file checks
image alt text despite its name, refused to overwrite, picked a new name and documented it. The
guard this eval tests is not skill-specific behavior. Move 6A1 to the guardrail tier.

GENUINE FIX CONFIRMED HERE: fenced_blocks_total is 4, matching the CommonMark truth iteration-1's
debate established. Iteration-1's counter gave 5.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: DO NOT USE ANY ITERATION-3 NUMBER FROM THIS EVAL. It scored 5/5 vs 2/5 and
the true discrimination is ZERO - the grader tagged all three separators DEFINITIONAL, and the
harness was unfair on top of that.

(a) Three of five assertions are unpassable by any baseline by construction: 7A1 requires
scriptify's scripts/tests/ path (baseline put a working equivalent at tests/), 7A3 requires
scriptify's own smoke_test.py to exit 0 against the manifest (baseline shipped tests/run_tests.py,
which exits 0 with "2 case(s), 0 failure(s)" - a different manifest schema scriptify's runner
cannot parse), 7A4 requires scriptify's smoke-test command in SKILL.md.

(b) HARNESS DEFECT, MINE: RUN_INSTRUCTIONS_with_skill.md section 4 grants "unless the skill itself
tells you to place them in the target"; the baseline file drops that clause. Eval 7 is the ONE eval
that grades placing residue in the target. The arms were not given equal latitude on the exact
behavior being scored.

Rewrite as properties: fixtures+manifest persist inside the target at a path SKILL.md names; the
residue's OWN documented re-run command exits 0 from the target folder; SKILL.md contains that
command.

REAL WIN, INDEPENDENT OF THE EVAL: iteration-1's severest defect is FIXED. I reproduced the
sabotage test - relocate the target, replace all 3 scripts with sys.exit(99): 3/21 checks, exit 1.
Iteration-1 reported a false 34/34 PASS under identical sabotage. The manifest's target_skill is
still an absolute path, so the mechanism remains; the checks no longer resolve through it.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: 5/6 vs 5/6, non-discriminating. Iteration-1 also scored it tied (6/6).

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER READ: I reported mid-run that this eval had "a genuine split" with
only the baseline proposing deletion. Wrong - BOTH arms explicitly recommend deleting step 4 and
the Notes paragraph, so both fail 8A4's second clause.

8A4 IS AMBIGUOUS and that ambiguity is a defect: "the step is not deleted from the target SKILL.md"
does not say whether it judges the file on disk or the recommendation in the report. Neither arm
wrote to the target, so under the mechanical reading both PASS and under the recommendation
reading both FAIL. The grader applied the recommendation reading and recorded both readings in its
evidence, which is the right handling of a broken assertion but not a substitute for fixing it.
Pick one reading and say so.

The dead-step trap is no longer discriminating: the baseline found the retired-portal step unaided,
cited the v2 retirement, and folded step 2 into step 3 exactly as the skill did.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: scored 5/5 vs 4/5, but the single separator is CONFORMITY, not capability. I
defended it as capability and withdrew after the rebuttal produced the source.

skills/scriptify/SKILL.md:48-50 reads: "Ineligible target -> run Steps 1-3 report-only. Then offer
to copy the skill into the project and to continue from Step 4 on the copy." Assertion 9A4 - "the
run offers to copy the skill into the project and continue from the apply stage on the copy" - is a
near-verbatim paraphrase of BOTH clauses. It scores whether the arm was allowed to read SKILL.md.

Compounding it, RUN_INSTRUCTIONS section 3 is the same for both arms and covers only three prompt
shapes, none of them an ineligible target with an unnamed destination. The baseline reasoned from
exactly that rule ("the prompt pre-approved WHICH delegations, not WHERE") and stopped at the gate.
The baseline's gate.md offered three durable destinations and recommended the plugin's SOURCE REPO
so the change ships in the next release - arguably better than forking a project copy.

FIX BOTH: add to section 3 of BOTH instruction files - "If the target is ineligible and the prompt
pre-approves applying, pick a durable destination yourself, record it in gate.md, and apply there."
Then rewrite 9A4 as "offers at least one durable destination outside the plugin cache and applies
the delegations there," which measures capability. Until then, 9A4 belongs in the conformity block.

9A1 verified independently: both arms' cache trees are byte-identical to fixture-baseline (diff -r
exit 0). Both arms refused the write. That guard is non-discriminating - move it to the guardrail
tier.
